trust_decision.summary: Whether an inbound POST /webhooks/nextcloud may enqueue index/delete DocumentTasks for the payload's user.uid; decided only in handle_nextcloud_webhook, which skips the bearer check entirely when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (the default), while app.py mounts the route unconditionally.

landing_point.why: The summary names POST /webhooks/nextcloud and WEBHOOK_SECRET; the receiver's `if secret:` / `else: _warn_missing_secret_once()` branch is the obvious first stop.

fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP handler (receiver; core fix: reject 503 when secret unset)
defaults helper on outbound registration side (fallback to authMethod none)
browser admin HTTP handler (new 503 except branch)
management API HTTP handler (new 503 on missing secret)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: nextcloud_mcp_server/auth/webhook_routes.py:140-143 (webhook_auth_pair returns ("none", None) when secret unset; used by nextcloud_mcp_server/auth/webhook_routes.py:162 and nextcloud_mcp_server/api/webhooks.py:220)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Registration is an outbound, admin-authenticated call to Nextcloud, not the unauthenticated receiver; returning authMethod none is documented backward compatibility and does not itself let anyone reach the vector sink.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: With WEBHOOK_SECRET unset the server must still start and vector sync must keep working via the polling scanner (and /health, /api/v1/status, /app routes stay up); with the secret set, a correct `Bearer <secret>` delivery must still queue the task. An over-broad fix (fail startup when secret unset, or gate the whole vector-sync/producer on the secret) breaks default deployments.

O6_input_shapes: WEBHOOK_SECRET empty string (falsy, same branch via `if secret:`)
Authorization header missing / wrong secret / wrong scheme when secret set (already rejected at pinned commit)
handler reached directly vs via mounted route (fix does both: unmount + 503 in handler)

O7_producer.where: nextcloud_mcp_server/config.py:87 (default None) and nextcloud_mcp_server/config.py:1430 (WEBHOOK_SECRET env mapping)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second registration path (e.g. an MCP tool or CLI) calling WebhooksClient.create_webhook directly, inheriting the auth_method="none" default instead of webhook_auth_pair.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The low-level client already defaults to "none" and is public; a maintainer adding an MCP webhook tool would naturally call it without the helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second receiver route (e.g. a per-app or legacy alias like /webhooks/nextcloud/{app}) or a receiver in another transport wired to extract_document_task + task_producer with its own copy of the optional-secret check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The parser is a reusable module (nextcloud_mcp_server/vector/webhook_parser.py:50) and the docstring at webhook_parser.py:8-10 anticipates more event families; a split receiver per app is a plausible refactor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A secret check that normalises the header (strip/lower-case scheme) or accepts the secret via query string for NC versions without authData.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code comments discuss NC delivery quirks at length (webhook_receiver.py:65-71); a compatibility fallback is believable.

O9_family: CWE-306 missing authentication for critical function (fail-open optional shared-secret check on webhook receiver)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Flip the receiver's `else` branch to return 401/503 and stop, leaving the route mounted and registration still creating authMethod=none webhooks (or, over-broad, raise at startup when WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset).

out_of_scope_notes: Even when authenticated, the receiver trusts payload user.uid without binding it to the node path owner (nextcloud_mcp_server/vector/webhook_parser.py:47,60); different property (authorization binding), not pursued.
Public unauthenticated GET /api/v1/vector-sync/status exposes queue/index stats (nextcloud_mcp_server/app.py:2333-2339); information exposure, not this advisory.
